title: Infernal Aura Strengths
heading: Infernal Auras
summary: Describes how an Infernal aura feels and what it does to people and the landscape at each band of aura strength, from subtle ill temper to Hell on earth.
quotes: Storyguides should ask for Personality rolls more frequently, to rein in these unusual impulses.

title: Infernal Auras in Play
heading: Infernal Auras in Play
summary: How an Infernal aura is centred on a focus, rises at night and on unholy days, changes on holy days in different faiths, coexists with stronger auras and erodes over time unless maintained.
quotes: All Infernal auras increase by one at night.
it takes a number of years equal to the strength of the Infernal aura for it to lose one point of strength
Whatever the source of an increase in an Infernal aura, it can never increase to a value greater than 10.

title: Formation of an Infernal Aura (Corruption Roll)
heading: The Formation of an Infernal Aura
summary: When a major sin is committed the storyguide makes a corruption roll to create, maintain or strengthen an Infernal aura; corruption rites let diabolists deliberately attempt this. Includes a worked example.
quotes: Corruption Roll: stress die + temporary Infernal aura strength
Ease Factor (to maintain Infernal aura): 3 + dominant aura strength
Ease Factor (to increase Infernal aura): 6 + dominant aura strength
A corruption rite cannot be successfully performed more than once a season.

title: Infernal Aura Examples Table
heading: Infernal Aura Examples
summary: A table of example locations and the Infernal aura rating each would typically have, useful as a benchmark for setting aura strengths.

title: Effects of an Infernal Aura
heading: Effects of an Infernal Aura
summary: Dominant Infernal auras impose the normal realm-interaction modifiers on Supernatural Powers and penalise recovery rolls for wounds, diseases and deprivation injuries for everyone inside.
quotes: suffers a penalty to the recovery roll for those wounds equal to the aura strength

title: Magical Reactions to the Infernal
heading: Magical Reactions to the Infernal
summary: Magic-realm beings avoid Infernal auras, and magi casting inside one may not notice the fatigue the aura costs them unless they pass a Perception roll.
quotes: Perception + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of (9 + aura strength)

title: Divine Reactions to the Infernal
heading: Divine Reactions to the Infernal
summary: Divine-affiliated characters sense the corruption of an Infernal aura more easily, and those with a Faith Score are immune to the extra effects of the specific kinds of Infernal aura.
quotes: receives a +3 bonus to all Perception rolls that would reveal the corrupt nature of the aura
characters with a Faith Score of at least 1 are immune to the additional effects imposed by different varieties of Infernal aura

title: Faerie Reactions to the Infernal
heading: Faerie Reactions to the Infernal
summary: Faeries are terrified of Infernal auras and rarely linger; their Supernatural Powers are weak and ineffectual there.
quotes: The expression of Faerie-derived Supernatural Powers is often weak and ineffectual in Infernal auras.

title: Tarnished Auras
heading: Tarnished Auras
summary: A tarnished aura is tied to one sinful Personality Trait that shifts the Traits of everyone inside and makes sinning in line with the tarnish a ritualised sin.
quotes: everyone within the aura suffers a modifier to Personality Traits equal to the strength of the aura

title: Corrupted Auras
heading: Corrupted Auras
summary: Corrupted auras are permanently tarnished auras of at least a minimum strength that add special sin-encouraging features, grouped as Debauched, Malevolent and Perfidious.

title: Debauched Auras
heading: Debauched Auras
summary: Corrupted auras of self-indulgence and indolence, with example features such as Personality rolls to leave or resist returning and a ban on spending Confidence Points.
quotes: with an Ease Factor equal to (3 + aura strength)
Ease Factor equal to (6 + aura strength)

title: Malevolent Auras
heading: Malevolent Auras
summary: Corrupted auras of cruelty and violence whose example effects add the aura strength to damage and to botch dice on physical activities, corrupt creatures and reopen old demonic wounds.
quotes: The aura strength is added to any Damage total.
a number of additional botch dice equal to the aura strength

title: Perfidious Auras
heading: Perfidious Auras
summary: Corrupted auras of deceit and betrayal that make lies harder to detect, give Infernal beings a temporary Confidence Point, and punish failed Confidence-modified rolls.
quotes: all attempts to spot a lie have the aura strength added to the Ease Factor

title: Infernal Regiones
heading: Infernal Regiones
summary: Infernal regiones are places God has left to the Infernal; Divine powers are suspended or penalised there and joy is impossible. Introduces the Tartaran and Abyssal types.
quotes: Holy Powers or Holy magic suffer a penalty to their rolls equal to the aura strength of the Infernal regio
related: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapter 3: Blessed by God

title: Tartaran Regiones
heading: Tartaran Regiones
summary: Regiones of hellfire: Fatigue becomes long-term, metal burns, flames do heavy fire damage, and sinful Personality Traits increase fire damage taken.
quotes: The flames, if touched directly, do anywhere from +5 to +35 fire damage

title: Abyssal Regiones
heading: Abyssal Regiones
summary: Regiones of privation: every Characteristic is reduced by the aura strength, and each day inside risks madness in the form of a temporary Flaw.
quotes: Every one of the eight Characteristics is reduced by a number of points equal to the strength of the aura in an Abyssal regio

title: Infernal Warping
heading: Infernal Warping
summary: Describes how Warping dominated by sin or Infernal contact produces sin-encouraging Flaws and Infernal Virtues at successive Warping Scores.
quotes: The character acquires a Minor Personality Flaw that reflects his obsession with sinful behavior.

title: Causes of Infernal Warping
heading: Causes of Infernal Warping
summary: Lists the ways a character gains Infernal Warping Points: ritualised sin, Infernal auras and regiones, Infernal Powers, and botches with unholy abilities.
quotes: every time a character ritualizes a sin to acquire Confidence Points, she gains a Warping Point
if the level of the Power is 30 or more, or if a demon spends 6 or more points of Might activating the power
One Warping Point is gained for each zero on a botch dice when using an unholy Power or Infernal Supernatural Ability.

title: Infernal Vis
heading: Infernal Vis
summary: Introduces Infernally tainted vis, which looks ordinary to Hermetic detection but endangers non-Infernal users, and the temporary Personality Trait imposed by prolonged contact with it.
quotes: The imposed trait either starts at a score of +1, or increases the trait by 1 if the magus already possesses it.
related: Chapter 4: The Infernal Legions, Common Powers

title: Vis Infesta
heading: Vis Infesta
summary: The mildest Infernal vis: it adds no extra botch dice beyond raw vis but makes any botch more severe, and experimentation in enchantments always yields the worst result.
quotes: one extra botch die per pawn of vis

title: Vis Sordida
heading: Vis Sordida
summary: Potent but dangerous Infernal vis that boosts casting totals and Source Quality at the cost of extra botch dice, and corrupts levels of effects in items prepared with it. Includes a worked enchanting example.
quotes: Each pawn of vis sordida used to enhance a casting total adds five to the roll, rather than the +2 of standard vis.
Using vis sordida always incurs three extra botch dice per pawn used
ten levels of effects in the item are corrupted for every pawn of vis sordida used

title: Vis Prava
heading: Vis Prava
summary: The vilest Infernal vis: any roll using it is automatically a zero with extra botch dice, studying from it causes Warping, and enchanting with it ruins the item; it is far better for Infernally aligned wizards.
quotes: rolling two extra botch dice for every pawn of vis prava used
vis prava offers a +5 bonus to Casting Totals per pawn employed

title: What Counts as Sin
heading: What is Sin?
summary: Explains how the storyguide judges whether an act is sinful: aiding the Infernal always is, while other acts depend on whether they are selfish or secret.

title: Types of Sin
heading: Types of Sin
summary: Distinguishes mortal sins from venial sins and notes that compelled or inadvertent acts are not sins, but dealing with the Infernal always stains the soul.

title: Sinful Traits
heading: Sinful Traits
summary: Optional method of tying each Personality Trait to a virtue or vice, with a table of the seven deadly sins and their related traits, so that sin-related rolls can be called for by category.
quotes: When dealing with opposing traits, treat the trait's value as negative.

title: Redemption
heading: Redemption
summary: Notes that any sinner, however corrupt, may escape Hell by truly repenting, with the means of absolution depending on faith.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapters 4, 5, 6

title: Infernal Influence
heading: Infernal Influence
summary: Infernalists inspire temporary sinful Personality Traits in willing followers through a season of personal influence or a short ceremony, with the strength set by a Presence + Leadership roll.
quotes: simple die + Presence + Leadership
Infernal Influence: simple die + Presence + Leadership
traits gained from personal influence can linger as long as a year, while those from ceremonial influence usually fade within about a week

title: Personality Flaws as Traits
heading: Personality Flaws
summary: For rules involving Personality Traits, treats a Personality Flaw as an equivalent Personality Trait so that it can be opposed by influence.
quotes: treat a Minor Personality Flaw as a +3 trait, and a Major Personality Flaw as a +6 trait

title: Tarnish
heading: Tarnish
summary: Infernalists tarnish an Infernal aura by giving it a sinful Personality Trait, using a stress roll on Presence + Leadership; the tarnish fades over time.
quotes: Tarnishing an aura: stress die + Presence + Leadership
its value decreases by one each morning

title: Gaining Confidence through Sin
heading: Gaining Confidence through Sin
summary: Characters with a sinful Personality Trait can earn Confidence Points by indulging in that sin for a season or through a ritualised act that also costs a Warping Point; even characters without Confidence can bank and spend the points.
quotes: Either activity yields a Confidence Point upon completion.
Generally speaking, venial sins are sufficient for traits of +3 or less

title: The Spiritual Form of a Demon
heading: The Spiritual Form of a Demon
summary: Rules for a demon in spirit form: unseen and unable to affect matter, immune to non-supernatural wounds and ageing, fast flying, and slain only by loss of Infernal Might.
quotes: spiritual demons may travel ten times faster than a human
can only be slain be effects that deplete its Infernal Might

title: The Physical Form of a Demon
heading: The Physical Form of a Demon
summary: Rules for a demon in coagulated physical form: it can interact with matter and be hurt or slain, heals and ages only in this form, and leaves a corpse that may hold vis.
quotes: typically a pawn for every magnitude of Infernal Might

title: Demonic Might Tables (Order and Rank)
heading: Demonic Might
summary: Tables giving the Infernal Might range and relative frequency of ranks for each of the nine demonic orders, plus the extra Infernal Might and equivalent Reputation each rank grants.
quotes: | Master | +5 | 3 |
| Prince | +20 | 9 |

title: Common Demonic Traits
heading: Common Demonic Traits
summary: Traits all demons share: Infernal Might, a defining sin as a Personality Trait, and an inability to display virtuous Personality Traits of their own free will.
quotes: A demon automatically fails personality rolls (ArM5, page 18) if succeeding would make it act in a virtuous manner.

title: Demonic Might: Order and Rank
heading: Demonic Might
summary: Explains that a demon's Infernal Might comes from its order plus a bonus for its rank, and that the two sources are indistinguishable in play.

title: Demonic Reputations
heading: Demonic Reputations
summary: Demons may have Infernal Reputations known to other demons and infernalists; the highest of these and the rank's equivalent Reputation gives the demon's Hierarchy score used when it is summoned.
quotes: The Hierarchy score of a demon is the highest of any Infernal Reputations it has

title: Demonic Characteristics
heading: Demonic Characteristics
summary: How to assign Characteristics to a demon: physical Characteristics are bought with points based on Infernal Might, mental ones with a small allotment, with a minimum physical score and no maximum. Includes example Infernal Reputations.
quotes: Demon Physical Characteristics points: Infernal Might
Demon Mental Characteristics points: 0 – 7 (possibly more for powerful demons)

title: Demonic Powers (Coagulation, Obsession, Envisioning, Possession)
heading: Demonic Powers
summary: The Powers common to all demons: Coagulation to form a body, Obsession to impose a sinful Personality Trait, Envisioning to send dreams and visions, and (for many) Possession of hosts via a separate Might Pool. Includes a worked Obsession example.
quotes: Manifesting a physical form takes a round for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon
with a score equal to the number of Might Points spent by the demon (maximum of 3)
A Supernatural Power (including spellcasting) requires 1 Might Point per magnitude

title: Demons and Magic
heading: Demons and Magic
summary: How Hermetic magic interacts with demons: it cannot pierce their deceptions, Second Sight is harder against them, they can be warded by Form, and Perdo Vim spells erode their Infernal Might.
quotes: this Ease Factor is increased by the magnitude of their Might
use the normal Ease Factor of 6 + magnitude of Might to pierce these deceptions
related: ArM5 p.80 Limit of Arcane Connections

title: Demonic Weaknesses
heading: Demonic Weaknesses
summary: Demons are hurt by relics and Divine worship objects and each has an individual weakness chosen from a list; characters with Infernal Lore can roll to know a demon's weakness.
quotes: Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9 + (Might / 5)
Subtract 3 from the Ease Factor if the demon is a member of a family
related: Realms of Power: The Divine, pp.41, 43

title: Religious Limitations on Demons
heading: Religious Limitations on Demons
summary: Calendar and faith-based restrictions on demons: Holy Saturday, the Jewish period between Yom Kippur and Sukkot, and the protection of a completed hajj.

title: True Names
heading: True Names
summary: True Names are the only Arcane Connection to a spirit that has no body; characters buy each with experience in Infernal Lore, and a known True Name aids penetration and synthemata research.
quotes: a +5 bonus to the Penetration Multiplier when penetrating an Infernal creature's Magic Resistance
Each True Name costs 5 experience points
related: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 9: Theurgy

title: Demons and Free Will
heading: Demons and Free Will
summary: Demons have free will but always choose evil; only those with a Confidence Score can put aside their passions to act rationally.

title: Demons, Auras, and Regiones
heading: Demons, Auras, and Regiones
summary: Governs how fast a demon regains Might Points normally, faster in Infernal auras, and not at all in a Divine aura.
quotes: Number of hours to restore all Might in Infernal aura: 24 – (2 x Infernal Aura)
A demon cannot regenerate any Might at all in a Divine aura.

title: The Infernal Hierarchy
heading: The Infernal Hierarchy
summary: Introduces the nine-order hierarchy of demons used to classify them, with the caveat that storyguides need not be constrained by it.

title: Infernal Ghosts
heading: Infernal Ghosts
summary: How to build an Infernal ghost as a demon: its role determines its order, and it lacks the Coagulation Power and physical statistics.
quotes: Infernal ghosts should be designed like any other demon, except that they have no Power of Coagulation

title: False Gods (Demonic Order)
heading: False Gods
summary: Order template for False Gods: Might limit, usual ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Shroud the Stench of the Pit, The Wealth of Nations and His Master's Voice.
quotes: Personality Traits:** Proud +6
for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon

title: Spirits of Deceit (Demonic Order)
heading: Spirits of Deceit
summary: Order template for Spirits of Deceit: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Change Form, Trust of the Innocent, Forked Tongue of the Serpent and The Serpent's Oracle.
quotes: The Size of the altered form is limited to whatever is natural for the species
An Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is allowed to resist the effect.

title: Vessels of Iniquity (Demonic Order)
heading: Vessels of Iniquity
summary: Order template for Vessels of Iniquity: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Form of Wickedness (a special Coagulation), Form of Man and Contagious Obsession.
quotes: A Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is needed every hour
For every victim who comes under the sway of the Obsession, the demon loses a point from its Might Pool

title: Avengers of Evil (Demonic Order)
heading: Avengers of Evil
summary: Order template for Avengers of Evil: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Punish the Sinner Power, whose wound depends on the victim's unatoned sin.
quotes: he suffers a Heavy wound if this Power penetrates his Magic Resistance
a number of points of damage equal to a simple die plus the sum total of all his sinful Personality Traits

title: Deluders (Demonic Order)
heading: Deluders
summary: Order template for Deluders: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Delusion and Duplicate the Magi's Technique-based spell effects.
quotes: A minor illusion which affects an Individual amount of material (such as the demon itself) costs one point
It cannot create any effect with a level greater than its Infernal Might, or duplicate Ritual effects.

title: Aerial Powers (Demonic Order)
heading: Aerial Powers
summary: Order template for Aerial Powers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Elemental Control and Recalcitrance, which inflates the demon's effective Might against control attempts.
quotes: at a cost of 1 Might Point per magnitude of effect
treats the demon's Might as if it were one-and-a-half times its actual Might

title: Furies (Demonic Order)
heading: Furies
summary: Order template for Furies: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Waxing Tide of Humors, Beserker Rage and Endurance of the Enraged.
quotes: must make a stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9
The Furies do not suffer from wound penalties, except on Defense totals.

title: Accusers (Demonic Order)
heading: Accusers
summary: Order template for Accusers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Betrayal of the Heart and Whispers Behind the Back.
quotes: This Power lasts for a month.

title: Tempters & Evil Spirits (Demonic Order)
heading: Tempters & Evil Spirits
summary: Order template for Tempters and Evil Spirits, the largest order: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and Flaws, with no Powers specific to the order.
quotes: Personality Traits:** Selfish +5

title: Checklist for Roleplaying Demons
heading: Checklist for Roleplaying Demons
summary: Lists behaviours demons cannot perform and those they can manage only by spending a Confidence Point, derived from their lack of the seven virtues.
quotes: Most demons cannot do the following, except with extreme effort (and spending a Confidence Point, which not all demons have):

title: A Life Lacking in Virtue (Demon Psychology)
heading: A Life Lacking in Virtue
summary: Demons lack all virtue and cannot be played like immoral humans; spending a Confidence Point lets a demon simulate a virtue for the duration of a situation.
quotes: the expenditure of a Confidence Point allows a demon to simulate a virtue in a particular instance

title: What are Demons?
heading: What are Demons?
summary: Defines what counts as a demon (any creature with an Infernal Might) and the celestial, terrestrial and Infernal-angel origins, which have no functional differences in play.
quotes: There are no functional differences between any of these groups.

title: Updating the Bestiary
heading: Updating the Bestiary
summary: Guidance for converting the demons in the core rulebook bestiary to the new rules by assigning each an order, the order's general traits and the Powers all demons share.

title: Example Infernal Reputations
heading: Example Infernal Reputations
summary: Table of example Infernal Reputation titles for each band of Reputation score, useful when giving a demon a Reputation.

title: Demons of God or Infernal Angels?
heading: Demons of God or Infernal Angels?
summary: Clarifies that Avengers of Evil and Accusers claiming to be angels are treated in game terms as demons with Infernal Might.
quotes: both Avengers of Evil and Accusers are demons, because they have Infernal Might rather than Divine Might
